chapters.title: The Kings of the South and the North
chapters.html:
Daniel 11

Persia and Greece

1"As for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to strengthen him and be a fortress for him.

2Now I will tell you the truth. Three more kings will arise in Persia, and the fourth will be far richer than all of them; and when he has grown strong through his riches, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.

3Then a mighty king will arise, who will rule with great dominion and do as he pleases.

4But as soon as he has arisen, his kingdom will be broken and divided toward the four winds of heaven, but not to his descendants, nor with the dominion he ruled with; for his kingdom will be uprooted and given to others besides these.

The South and the North

5Then the king of the south will grow strong, but one of his princes will grow stronger than he and will rule, and his dominion will be a great dominion.

6At the end of some years they will make an alliance, and the daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement. But she will not keep the strength of her arm, and he and his arm will not stand; she will be given up, with those who brought her, her father, and the one who supported her in those times.

7But a branch from her roots will arise in his place. He will come against the army and enter the fortress of the king of the north, and he will deal with them and prevail.

8He will also carry off to Egypt as plunder their gods, with their cast images and their precious vessels of silver and gold; and for some years he will keep away from the king of the north.

9Then he will enter the kingdom of the king of the south and return to his own land.

10His sons will stir themselves up and gather a multitude of great forces, and one of them will surely come and overflow and pass through; then he will wage war again, up to his fortress.

11Then the king of the south, enraged, will go out and fight with him, with the king of the north. He will raise a great multitude, but the multitude will be given into his hand.

12When the multitude is carried off, his heart will be lifted up; he will bring down tens of thousands, but he will not prevail.

13For the king of the north will again raise a multitude, greater than the first, and at the end of the times, after some years, he will surely come with a great army and much equipment.

14In those times many will rise against the king of the south, and the violent men of your own people will lift themselves up to fulfill the vision, but they will stumble.

15Then the king of the north will come and throw up a siege mound and take a fortified city, and the forces of the south will not stand, not even his choice troops; there will be no strength to stand.

16He who comes against him will do as he pleases, and no one will stand before him; he will stand in the beautiful land, with destruction in his hand.

17He will set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, bringing terms of agreement, and he will carry them out; he will give him a daughter in marriage, to destroy it; but it will not stand or be his.

18Then he will turn his face to the coastlands and capture many; but a commander will put an end to his insolence, and more than that, he will turn his insolence back on him.

19Then he will turn his face back toward the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and fall and not be found.

20Then in his place one will arise who sends an exactor through the glory of the kingdom; but within a few days he will be broken, though not in anger or in battle.

The Contemptible King

21In his place will arise a contemptible man, on whom royal majesty has not been conferred. He will come in while they are at ease and seize the kingdom by smooth words.

22Overwhelming forces will be swept away before him and broken, and the prince of the covenant as well.

23After an alliance is made with him he will act deceitfully; he will rise and become strong with a small nation.

24While they are at ease he will enter the richest parts of the province and do what neither his fathers nor his fathers' fathers did, scattering plunder, spoil and goods among them. He will devise plans against fortresses, but only for a time.

25He will stir up his strength and his courage against the king of the south with a great army, and the king of the south will wage war with a very great and mighty army; but he will not stand, for plans will be devised against him.

26Those who eat his royal food will break him; his army will be swept away, and many will fall slain.

27The two kings, their hearts set on evil, will speak lies at one table; but it will not succeed, for the end is still to come at the appointed time.

28He will return to his land with great wealth, but his heart will be set against the holy covenant; he will act, and return to his land.

29At the appointed time he will come again into the south, but this time it will not be as it was before.

30Ships of Kittim will come against him, and he will lose heart and turn back. He will rage against the holy covenant and take action; he will turn back and pay heed to those who forsake the holy covenant.

31Forces from him will rise up and profane the sanctuary, the fortress, and take away the continual offering, and set up the loathsome thing that desolates.

32Those who act wickedly against the covenant he will corrupt with smooth words; but the people who know their God will stand firm and take action.

33The wise among the people will give understanding to the many, though for some days they will stumble by sword and flame, by captivity and plunder.

34When they stumble, they will receive a little help, and many will join them with smooth words.

35Some of the wise will stumble, to refine, purify and make them white, until the time of the end, for it is still to come at the appointed time.

The King Who Exalts Himself

36The king will do as he pleases. He will exalt himself and magnify himself above every god, and against the God of gods he will speak astonishing things. He will prosper until the wrath is complete, for what has been decreed will be done.

37He will pay no heed to the gods of his fathers, or to the one desired by women; he will pay no heed to any god, for he will magnify himself above all.

38Instead, he will honor the god of fortresses in its place; a god his fathers did not know he will honor with gold and silver, with precious stones and precious things.

39He will deal with the strongest fortresses with the help of a foreign god. Those who acknowledge him he will load with honor; he will make them rulers over the many and divide the land for a price.

40At the time of the end the king of the south will charge at him, and the king of the north will storm against him with chariots and horsemen and many ships. He will enter the lands, overflow them and pass through.

41He will enter the beautiful land, and many will stumble; but these will escape from his hand: Edom, Moab and the chief of the sons of Ammon.

42He will stretch out his hand against the lands, and the land of Egypt will not escape.

43He will rule over the hidden treasures of gold and silver and all the precious things of Egypt, and the Libyans and the Cushites will follow in his steps.

44But reports from the east and the north will alarm him, and he will go out in great fury to destroy many and destroy them completely.

45He will pitch his royal tents between the seas and the beautiful holy mountain; yet he will come to his end, and no one will help him.

Notes

  • v1 "in the first year of Darius the Mede" — the man in linen is still speaking, from 10:21. Him is most likely Michael, the last one named: the speaker stood by Michael then, as Michael stands by him now. It could also be Darius. The Greek has in the first year of Cyrus.

  • vv2–45 the kings — after Persia and Greece (vv2–4), not one king in the chapter is named. They are the king of the south and the king of the north, and the only places named are Egypt, Kittim, Edom, Moab, Ammon, Libya and Cush. Ma'oz, fortress, runs through the chapter, from the speaker's own help in the first year of Darius (v1) to the god of fortresses (v38).

  • v7 "a branch from her roots" — netser shorasheha, the words of Isaiah's king from Jesse's line, a branch from his roots will bear fruit (Isaiah 11:1), here used of a southern king's heir.

  • v22 "the prince of the covenant" — negid berit. Nagid, prince, is the word of 9:25–26, an anointed one, a prince and the prince who is to come. Who the prince of the covenant is, the chapter does not say.

  • v26 "Those who eat his royal food" — okhlei fat-bago, the pat-bag that Daniel would not eat at Nebuchadnezzar's court (1:5, 8). The king is broken by the men who eat at his table.

  • v30 "Ships of Kittim" — Balaam's last oracle: Ships shall come from the coast of Kittim, and they shall afflict Asshur (Numbers 24:24), tsim mi-yad Kittim; here tsiyyim Kittim.

  • v31 "the loathsome thing that desolates" — ha-shiqquts meshomem, with the continual offering taken away, as in 8:11–13 and 9:27, and again in 12:11. The Greek has an abomination made desolate; Jesus quotes it as the abomination of desolation (Matthew 24:15).

  • vv33–35 "The wise among the people… to refine, purify and make them white" — maskilei am, who give understanding to the many. They return at the end of the book, where those who are wise will shine and many will be purified, made white and refined (12:3, 10).

  • vv36–39 "against the God of gods… the one desired by women… the god of fortresses" — the king speaks as the little horn did, words against the Most High (7:25), and stands against the Prince of princes (8:25). Chemdat nashim, the desire of women, is obscure: a god whom women love, or the love of women itself. Eloah ma'uzzim, the god of fortresses, is left untranslated in the Greek, Maōzin.

  • v45 "he will come to his end, and no one will help him" — he dies as the horn of 8:25 was broken, not by any hand; no battle is described. The faithful were given a little help (v34); he is given none.

chapters.title: The Time of the End
chapters.html:
Daniel 12

Those Who Sleep in the Dust

1"At that time Michael, the great prince who stands over the sons of your people, will arise. There will be a time of distress such as has not been since there was a nation until that time. But at that time your people will be delivered, everyone who is found written in the book.

2Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting abhorrence.

3Those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the expanse, and those who make the many righteous, like the stars, forever and ever.

4But you, Daniel, shut up the words and seal the book until the time of the end. Many will run to and fro, and knowledge will increase."

How Long?

5Then I, Daniel, looked, and two others were standing there, one on this bank of the river and one on that bank.

6One said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, "How long until the end of these wonders?"

7I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river: he raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swore by Him who lives forever that it would be for a time, times and half a time, and that when the shattering of the power of the holy people comes to an end, all these things will be finished.

8I heard, but I did not understand. So I said, "My lord, what will be the outcome of these things?"

9He said, "Go, Daniel, for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.

10Many will be purified, made white and refined; but the wicked will act wickedly, and none of the wicked will understand, but those who are wise will understand.

11From the time the continual offering is taken away and the loathsome thing that desolates is set up, there will be one thousand two hundred and ninety days.

12Blessed is the one who waits and reaches one thousand three hundred and thirty-five days.

13But you, go your way until the end. You will rest, and you will stand up for your lot at the end of the days."

Notes

  • v1 "a time of distress… written in the book" — Jesus uses this verse: there will be great affliction, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now (Matthew 24:21). The book is the one Moses asked to be blotted out of, Your book that You have written, and God answered, Whoever has sinned against Me, him I will blot out of My book (Exodus 32:32–33).

  • v2 "Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake" — le-chayyei olam, to everlasting life, a phrase found only here in the Hebrew Bible. Isaiah had said it in a song, Awake and sing for joy, you who dwell in the dust! (Isaiah 26:19). Dir'on, abhorrence, is found only here and in the last verse of Isaiah, they will be an abhorrence to all flesh (Isaiah 66:24).

  • v3 "Those who are wise… those who make the many righteous" — ha-maskilim and matsdiqei ha-rabbim, the words of Isaiah's servant: My servant will act wisely (yaskil, Isaiah 52:13), and the righteous one, My servant, will make the many righteous (yatsdiq… la-rabbim, Isaiah 53:11). The wise were the ones who stumble by sword and flame (11:33). They shine like the expanse, raqia, the heaven of the second day of creation (Genesis 1:6–8).

  • v4 "Many will run to and fro, and knowledge will increase" — yeshotetu rabbim, the verb Amos uses of people running to and fro to seek the word of the LORD and not finding it (Amos 8:12). The Greek reads until many are taught and knowledge increases.

  • vv5–7 "the river… swore by Him who lives forever" — the river of 10:4 was nahar; here it is ye'or, the word used for the Nile, where Pharaoh stood in his dream (Genesis 41:1). The man raises both hands, as God says in the Song of Moses, I lift up My hand to heaven and say: As I live forever (Deuteronomy 32:40). Revelation's angel raises his hand and swears the same way (Revelation 10:5–6).

  • v7 "a time, times and half a time" — mo'ed mo'adim va-chetsi, the Hebrew of the Aramaic time, times and half a time (7:25).

  • vv11–12 "one thousand two hundred and ninety… one thousand three hundred and thirty-five days" — two numbers, thirty and forty-five days apart, given without explanation after the 2,300 evenings and mornings of 8:14. Blessed is the one who waits is ashrei, the first word of the Psalms, Blessed is the man (Psalm 1:1).

  • v13 "You will rest, and you will stand up for your lot at the end of the days" — tanuach, rest, and ta'amod, stand, the verb of Michael who will arise (v1). Goral, lot, is the word for a share of the land given by lot, as in Joshua, The lot of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin came up (Joshua 18:11). Le-qets ha-yamin, at the end of the days, spells days with the Aramaic ending -in.

chapters.title: Susanna
chapters.html:
Daniel 13

The Two Elders

1There was a man living in Babylon whose name was Joakim.

2He took a wife named Susanna, the daughter of Hilkiah, a very beautiful woman who feared the Lord.

3Her parents were righteous, and they had taught their daughter according to the law of Moses.

4Joakim was very rich, and he had a garden next to his house. The Jews used to come to him, because he was the most honored of them all.

59Daniel said to him, "Right! You too have lied against your own head, for the messenger of God is waiting with his sword to saw you in two, to destroy you both."

chapters.title: Bel and the Dragon
chapters.html:
Daniel 14

Bel

1King Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus the Persian received his kingdom.

2Daniel was the king's companion and was honored above all his friends.

3The Babylonians had an idol named Bel, and every day they spent on it twelve measures of fine flour, forty sheep and six jars of wine.

4The king worshipped it and went every day to bow down to it, but Daniel bowed down to his own God. The king said to him, "Why do you not bow down to Bel?"

5He said, "Because I do not worship idols made by hands, but the living God, who created heaven and earth and has dominion over all flesh."

6The king said to him, "Do you not think Bel is a living god? Do you not see how much he eats and drinks every day?"

7Daniel laughed and said, "Do not be deceived, O king. This is clay inside and bronze outside, and it has never eaten anything."

8The king was angry. He called his priests and said to them, "If you do not tell me who is eating up these provisions, you will die.

9But if you show that Bel is eating them, Daniel will die, because he has blasphemed against Bel." Daniel said to the king, "Let it be as you say."

10There were seventy priests of Bel, besides their wives and children. The king went with Daniel into the temple of Bel.

11The priests of Bel said, "We are going outside. You, O king, set out the food and mix the wine and set it there; then shut the door and seal it with your signet ring.

12When you come in the morning, if you do not find that Bel has eaten everything, let us die; otherwise Daniel, who is telling lies about us."

13They were unconcerned, for they had made a hidden entrance under the table, and through it they used to go in regularly and consume the offerings.

14When they had gone out, the king set out the food for Bel. Then Daniel ordered his servants to bring ashes, and they sifted them over the whole temple in the presence of the king alone. Then they went out, shut the door, sealed it with the king's signet ring, and went away.

15In the night the priests came as usual, with their wives and children, and they ate everything and drank it all.

16Early in the morning the king rose, and Daniel with him.

17The king said, "Are the seals unbroken, Daniel?" He said, "They are unbroken, O king."

18As soon as the doors were opened, the king looked at the table and cried out with a loud voice, "You are great, O Bel, and there is no deceit in you at all!"

19But Daniel laughed and held the king back from going in, and he said, "Look at the floor, and see whose footprints these are."

20The king said, "I see the footprints of men and women and children."

21Then the king was angry, and he arrested the priests with their wives and children, and they showed him the secret doors through which they used to come in and consume what was on the table.

22The king put them to death, and he handed Bel over to Daniel, who destroyed it and its temple.

The Dragon

23There was also a great dragon, which the Babylonians worshipped.

24The king said to Daniel, "You cannot say that this is not a living god. So bow down to it."

25Daniel said, "I will bow down to the Lord my God, for He is the living God.

26But you, O king, give me permission, and I will kill the dragon without sword or club." The king said, "I give it to you."

27Then Daniel took pitch, fat and hair, boiled them together and made cakes, and he put them into the dragon's mouth. The dragon ate them and burst open. Daniel said, "See what you have been worshipping!"

28When the Babylonians heard it, they were furious and turned against the king, saying, "The king has become a Jew. He has pulled down Bel, killed the dragon and slaughtered the priests."

29They came to the king and said, "Hand Daniel over to us, or we will kill you and your household."

30The king saw that they were pressing him hard, and under compulsion he handed Daniel over to them.

The Lions' Den Again

31They threw him into the den of lions, and he was there six days.

32There were seven lions in the den, and every day they had been given two human bodies and two sheep; but now nothing was given them, so that they would devour Daniel.

33Now the prophet Habakkuk was in Judea. He had made a stew and broken bread into a bowl, and he was going into the field to take it to the reapers.

34The messenger of the Lord said to Habakkuk, "Take the meal you have to Babylon, to Daniel, in the den of lions."

35Habakkuk said, "Lord, I have never seen Babylon, and I do not know the den."

36Then the messenger of the Lord took him by the crown of his head, and carrying him by the hair of his head, set him down in Babylon above the den, with the rushing of his spirit.

37Habakkuk called out, "Daniel! Daniel! Take the meal that God has sent you."

38Daniel said, "You have remembered me, O God, and You have not forsaken those who love You."

39So Daniel got up and ate, and the messenger of God at once returned Habakkuk to his own place.

40On the seventh day the king came to mourn for Daniel. He came to the den and looked in, and Daniel was sitting there.

41He cried out with a loud voice, "You are great, O Lord, God of Daniel, and there is no other besides You!"

42Then he pulled Daniel out, and he threw into the den those who had tried to destroy him, and they were devoured at once before his eyes.

Notes

  • v1 "King Astyages… Cyrus the Persian" — this chapter, like chapter 13, has no Hebrew or Aramaic; the text is Theodotion's Greek. The Old Greek opens differently: From the prophecy of Habakkuk son of Joshua, of the tribe of Levi. There was a man, a priest, whose name was Daniel son of Abal, a companion of the king of Babylon. The king there is not named.

  • vv3, 22 "Bel" — the god Isaiah mocked, Bel bows down; Nebo stoops (Isaiah 46:1), and Jeremiah's word against him: I will punish Bel in Babylon, and take out of his mouth what he has swallowed (Jeremiah 51:44). In this chapter the swallowing is found out.

  • vv5–7 "idols made by hands… clay inside and bronze outside" — the psalm's idols, the work of human hands (Psalm 115:4), against the living God, who created heaven and earth. A god of clay and bronze, like the feet of iron and clay on which the statue fell (2:33–34).

  • vv11–17 the sealed door — the king seals the temple with his signet ring, as the stone on the lions' den was sealed in chapter 6 (6:17). The ashes on the floor keep a record the seals cannot.

  • v23 "a great dragon" — drakōn, the Greek word for the sea monster of the prophets: in Greek, Isaiah's dragon that is in the sea is drakōn (Isaiah 27:1), and so is the sea monster that swallowed Jerusalem in Jeremiah, he has swallowed me like a sea monster (Jeremiah 51:34).

  • vv31–42 the second den — a second time in the lions' den: here for six days, with seven lions kept hungry, and the king comes on the seventh day. As in 6:24, those who brought it about are thrown in and devoured.

  • vv33–39 Habakkuk — the prophet whose book comes later in this canon. By the hair of his head: Ezekiel was carried the same way, He stretched out the form of a hand and took me by a lock of my head; and the spirit lifted me up (Ezekiel 8:3).

  • v41 "there is no other besides You" — the words of Isaiah 45:5, I am the LORD, and there is no other; besides Me there is no God, in the mouth of a Persian king, as Darius praised the living God in 6:26.
